features.description: New internal/ai/ollama/idlereader.go + idlereader_test.go. A deadline-resetting io.ReadCloser (NOT a bare Reader - StreamStep's `defer httpResp.Body.Close()` at streamstep.go:100 is what stops the watchdog; a bare Reader loses the underlying Close and leaves the timer armed). First-Read deadline = TTFT window; every Read returning n>0 resets to the idle window. A blocked Read cannot interrupt itself, so the watchdog calls a supplied context.CancelFunc and the transport fails the pending Read. Which-window-fired is recorded via an atomic CAS (first writer wins) so the surfaced error is typed. Close() stops the timer/goroutine THEN closes the underlying body, idempotent. Typed sentinels distinguishable by errors.Is: ErrTTFTTimeout, ErrIdleTimeout, ErrStreamDeadlineExceeded, ErrStreamDeadlineInvalid. A RoundTripper that wraps resp.Body. Three resolvers: AILANG_OLLAMA_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC (default 120), AILANG_OLLAMA_TTFT_TIMEOUT_SEC (default 600), and a SEPARATE ollamaStreamHardDeadline() reading AILANG_OLLAMA_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SEC with default 3600 and <=0 REJECTED. ollamaV1Timeout() is NOT touched. Base transport built ONCE via sync.Once, cloned from http.DefaultTransport, carrying ResponseHeaderTimeout = TTFT window - never mutate DefaultTransport, never a fresh &http.Transport{} per call (IdleConnTimeout 0 = no limit = fd leak). ZERO call sites are added, so runtime behaviour is unchanged by construction.
acceptance_criteria: AC-M1.1 (doc S2 mechanics; mutation R2): `go test -count=1 -v ./internal/ai/ollama -run TestIdleReader` - an io.Pipe case writes 3 chunks then goes silent; Read must return an error satisfying errors.Is(err, ErrIdleTimeout) within idle+slack (test windows <=200ms via direct struct construction, not env). BASE AT 3e1f63f7a: rc=0, '=== RUN' count 0, '[no tests to run]' - VACUOUSLY GREEN. Pass requires rc=0 AND '=== RUN' >= 6 AND a '--- PASS' per named subtest. AC-M1.3 (which-window-fired is preserved): three cases assert three DISTINCT sentinels - ErrTTFTTimeout, ErrIdleTimeout, ErrStreamDeadlineExceeded - using errors.Is, PLUS pairwise NON-equality assertions (e.g. !errors.Is(idleErr, ErrTTFTTimeout)), so returning one generic error for all three cannot pass. features.description: internal/ai/ollama/step.go + step_test.go. (1) Capture outerCtx := ctx at step.go:265, BEFORE `ctx, cancel := ollamaCallContext(ctx)` at :266 - this is REFUTATION #1's fix; the flag-off branch and the native path keep using the 300s-bounded ctx byte-for-byte. (2) Streaming branch under os.Getenv("AILANG_OLLAMA_V1_STREAM")=="1": streamCtx, cancel, cfgErr := streamCallContext(outerCtx), which resolves ollamaStreamHardDeadline() and returns cfgErr BEFORE any HTTP request is made on <=0, otherwise context.WithTimeout(outerCtx, hard). (3) openai.NewClient(... WithHTTPClient(&http.Client{Timeout: 0, Transport: idleTransport(streamCancel)})) - Timeout 0 per V12, the bound is the context. (4) v1.StreamStep(streamCtx, &r2, onChunk) - onChunk is NOT nil (escalation E-1); in M2 it is a byte/delta counter for the debug log, and M3 gives it the parity job. (5) Error mapping with EXPLICIT precedence: (a) a fired window recorded by the wrapper's atomic CAS wins; (b) else streamCtx.Err()==context.DeadlineExceeded => ErrStreamDeadlineExceeded; (c) else classify normally. Precedence must be explicit because the idle timer can race the hard deadline. (6) Per-request debug logging of max inter-chunk gap, TTFT, total duration, AND the EFFECTIVE hard deadline read back from streamCtx.Deadline() (read back, never the configured value) - that last field is what makes AC-M2.4 possible.
